issue.author: internal-review-repo
issue.body:
Review of delivery at experiment-repo b35dd368f32a.

Verified: timings.csv has 50 rows (2 algorithms x 5 sizes x 5 reps); I reran analyze.py on it and it reproduces fits.json exactly (1.867 +/- 0.055, 0.925 +/- 0.049). Algorithms are asserted against sorted(); the figure shows raw points, both fits, labelled axes and a legend, and it matches the report. The report's treatment of merge sort exponent < 1 and the shallow 1000->2000 step is honest and sound.

One finding: the objective asks for a **one-page report**. report.md is ~700 words with a table, a full-size figure and a long Findings section, which will not fit on one page.

Requested change: trim report.md to one page (about 350-450 words plus the table and the figure). Keep both exponents with SE/CI, the fit method, and the key caveats (merge sort < 1 is an artefact of the shallow 1000->2000 step vs the ~1.1 expected for n log n; CIs cover scatter only). Move the replicate-run details and the per-statistic robustness check into a separate file outside report.md (e.g. notes_replicate.md, or keep the JSONs) and refer to it in one line.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body: Measure how insertion sort and merge sort scale with input size in pure Python. Time each algorithm on random integer lists of sizes 250, 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000, five repetitions each, and fit the exponent of time against size on a log-log scale for each algorithm. The timing run takes a few minutes, so run it as a background job on the local-compute resource (ht-resource run) rather than inside your turn, and continue when it ends. Deliver the script, the raw timings as CSV, one log-log figure and a one-page report with the two fitted exponents.
issue.title: Research objective
